title: Bridge Street in Heywood closed over fears wind could cause building to collapse
excerpt: Firefighters, police and Rochdale Council responded to concerns about a derelict building. The structure was still standing in the latest report.
body:
Emergency services attended Bridge Street in Heywood on Saturday evening after concerns that strong winds could cause a derelict building to collapse, according to the Manchester Evening News.

The newspaper's update at 9.20pm BST on 24 October reported that the area had been made safe, the building was still standing and firefighters remained at the scene.

Update: 11.31pm BST, Saturday 24 October 2026

Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service, in a statement carried by the Manchester Evening News, said one engine from Heywood was sent at about 6.30pm. Crews worked with Greater Manchester Police and Rochdale Council to secure the area. They were still attending when that statement was issued.

No reopening time or information about injuries has been confirmed in the reports reviewed. The precise building has not been identified in the material available to Rochdale Daily.

Earlier report: 9.25pm BST, Saturday 24 October 2026

Roch Valley Radio reported that Bridge Street was closed by emergency services. Its photographs showed a police cordon, a marked police car blocking access and a fire engine.

Anyone approaching the closure should follow directions from emergency services and allow extra time for their journey. Further confirmed information about the restrictions will be added to this article.
